question: What was the key contribution of Baikuntha Shukla in the Indian freedom struggle?
solution:
The correct answer is __**He assassinated a government approver**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Baikuntha Shukla** played a key role in the Indian freedom struggle by assassinating **Phanindranath Ghosh**, a government approver who betrayed revolutionaries like Bhagat Singh, Rajguru, and Sukhdev.
 
• Phanindranath Ghosh had turned into a British informant, leading to the arrest and execution of several revolutionary leaders.
 
• Shukla carried out the assassination on **9 November 1932** to uphold the revolutionary spirit and discourage betrayal within the freedom movement.
 
• He was associated with the revolutionary organization **Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA)**, which was instrumental in fighting British colonial rule through armed resistance.
 
• Baikuntha Shukla was arrested, tried, and eventually hanged on **14 May 1934**, making him one of the youngest martyrs of the Indian independence movement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Champaran Satyagraha (Option 1):**

 
 
• The Champaran Satyagraha of 1917 was led by **Mahatma Gandhi** and marked his first significant involvement in the Indian freedom struggle.
 
• It was initiated to address the grievances of farmers in Bihar who were forced to grow indigo under oppressive conditions imposed by British landlords.
 
• This non-violent movement resulted in the abolition of the exploitative tinkathia system and marked Gandhi's emergence as a mass leader in India.
 
 
 
• **Protest against Simon Commission (Option 2):**
 
 
• The Simon Commission, formed in 1927, was a British initiative to review constitutional reforms in India, but it lacked Indian representation.
 
• The commission was met with widespread protests, and the slogan "**Simon Go Back**" became popular.
 
• Lala Lajpat Rai suffered fatal injuries during a protest against the commission in 1928, further igniting nationalist sentiments.
 
 
 
• **Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA) (Option 4):**
 
 
• The HSRA was a revolutionary organization formed in 1928 by leaders like **Chandrasekhar Azad, Bhagat Singh, and Sukhdev**.
 
• The group aimed to overthrow British rule through direct action, including armed resistance and political assassinations.
 
• HSRA members carried out significant actions, such as the assembly bombing in 1929 and the assassination of British police officer J.P. Saunders in 1928.
 
 
 
• **Baikuntha Shukla and the Revolutionary Movement:**
 
 
• Baikuntha Shukla's actions reflect the dedication and sacrifices of revolutionaries who believed in armed struggle as a means to achieve independence.
 
• His martyrdom serves as a reminder of the diverse strategies employed in India's fight against colonial oppression, ranging from non-violent satyagraha to armed resistance.
